title: One event per moment

blocks.text: Two feeds report the same events, each in its own zone, so one moment can arrive as `2024-03-15T12:00-04:00[America/New_York]` and again as `2024-03-15T16:00Z[Europe/London]`.

Write `Events.distinctMoments(List<ZonedDateTime> events)`. It keeps the first event for each **moment on the timeline**, and drops every later event at that same moment, whatever zone or offset it is written in. Events at the same wall-clock time in different zones are different moments. The events it keeps stay in **the order they came in**.

rows: `12:00 New York`, `13:00 New York`, `12:00 New York`
both: half a second apart is another moment

cases.says: An event repeated in the same zone is kept once, the first time it appears.
Noon in New York, 16:00 in London, 16:00 UTC and 12:00-04:00 are one moment, kept once.
Noon in New York, noon in London and noon in Tokyo are three different moments.
The kept events stay in their input order, even when a later moment came first.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: equals() on ZonedDateTime also compares the zone, so the same moment is found with isEqual() or by comparing toInstant().
ZoneId.of("UTC") is a region that is not equal to ZoneOffset.UTC, though both name the same moments.
